learning_objective: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a square matrix and interpret their geometric meaning as scaling factors and invariant directions under a linear transformation.
Decompose a matrix using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and apply it to dimensionality reduction and low-rank approximation problems.
Represent a linear transformation as a matrix and describe how it maps vectors between spaces, including identifying stretching, rotation, and reflection.
Determine whether a given set of vectors forms a vector space or subspace by verifying closure under addition and scalar multiplication.
Calculate the rank and null space of a matrix and use them to determine the solution structure of a system of linear equations.
Derive the least squares solution to an overdetermined system and apply it to fit a linear model to data by minimizing residual error.
Apply the Gram-Schmidt process to produce an orthonormal basis and use orthogonal projections to decompose vectors within a subspace.
Construct a transition matrix for a Markov chain and compute the steady-state distribution by finding its dominant eigenvector.
Evaluate the determinant of a matrix to determine invertibility and use it to understand how a transformation scales area or volume.
Construct a covariance matrix from a dataset and interpret its diagonal and off-diagonal entries in terms of variance and feature correlation.
Compute partial derivatives of a multivariable function and assemble them into a gradient vector that points in the direction of steepest ascent.
Apply the first and second derivative tests to locate and classify local maxima, minima, and saddle points of a differentiable function.
Solve a first-order ordinary differential equation using separation of variables and interpret the solution as a model of a dynamic system.
Evaluate definite integrals using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and interpret the result as the net signed area under a curve.
Construct a Taylor series expansion of a smooth function around a point and use it to approximate the function's value near that point.
Use Lagrange multipliers to find the extrema of a multivariable function subject to an equality constraint.
Implement the gradient descent update rule and explain how step size and gradient magnitude jointly determine convergence toward a local minimum.
Set up and solve a related rates problem by differentiating an implicit relationship with respect to time to find an unknown rate of change.
Apply the Fourier transform to decompose a time-domain signal into its frequency components and interpret the resulting spectrum.
Evaluate the limit of a function at a point using formal limit laws and determine whether the function is continuous at that point.
Formulate null and alternative hypotheses for a given research question, select an appropriate test statistic, and make a reject/fail-to-reject decision based on the p-value.
Construct a confidence interval for a population mean or proportion and correctly interpret it as a range that captures the true parameter with a stated level of confidence.
Fit a simple or multiple linear regression model to data, interpret the coefficients, and assess model fit using R-squared and residual diagnostics.
State the Central Limit Theorem and use it to justify why the sampling distribution of the mean approaches normality as sample size increases, regardless of population shape.
Distinguish between Type I and Type II errors in hypothesis testing, explain the trade-off between them, and relate each to the concepts of significance level and statistical power.
Compare probability, stratified, and convenience sampling methods and identify how each can introduce or reduce selection bias in a study.
Conduct a one-way ANOVA to test whether the means of three or more groups differ significantly, and interpret the F-statistic and associated p-value.
Explain why a strong correlation between two variables does not imply a causal relationship, and identify confounding variables or alternative explanations.
Apply Bayes' theorem to update a prior probability distribution with new evidence and interpret the resulting posterior distribution.
Decompose a time series into trend, seasonality, and residual components and apply a forecasting method such as exponential smoothing.
Calculate conditional probabilities using the definition P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B) and apply the law of total probability to partition complex probability problems.
Apply Bayes' theorem to reverse conditional probabilities and update the likelihood of a hypothesis given new observed evidence.
Define discrete and continuous random variables, identify their probability distributions, and compute probabilities using PMFs and PDFs.
State the Law of Large Numbers and use it to explain why the sample mean converges to the population mean as the number of trials increases.
Compute the expected value of a discrete or continuous random variable and interpret it as the long-run average outcome of a random process.
Calculate the variance and standard deviation of a random variable from its distribution and interpret them as measures of spread around the mean.
Distinguish between statistical independence and zero correlation, and determine whether two events or variables satisfy each condition.
Model the number of events occurring in a fixed interval using a Poisson distribution and verify when the Poisson process assumptions are satisfied.
Design a Monte Carlo simulation to estimate a probability or expected value by generating random samples and computing sample statistics.
Calculate the Shannon entropy of a discrete probability distribution and interpret it as a measure of uncertainty or information content.
